lines: 先做一个思想实验：我说，我养了一只……
Let's start with a thought experiment. I say: I keep a pet...
你脑子里大概已经跳出了「猫」或者「狗」。
Your mind has probably already jumped to "cat" or "dog".
几乎不可能是「微波炉」。
It is almost certainly not "microwave."
为什么？因为你读过很多中文，知道这里常出现哪些词。
Why? Because you have read a lot of Chinese, and you know which words tend to appear here.
你对语言的把握，至少有一部分，就表现为对下一个词的预期。
At least part of your grasp of language shows up as an expectation about the next word.
这一章，我们把这种预期，变成一个可以计算的东西。
In this chapter, we turn that expectation into something computable.

scenes.zh: 一台只做一件事的机器
lines: 假设模型的词表里只有四个词：猫、狗、鱼、车。
Suppose the model's vocabulary has only four words: cat, dog, fish, car.
对于刚才那句话，模型给出的不是答案，而是一组概率。
For that sentence, the model does not give an answer. It gives a set of probabilities.
四个数字加起来等于一，因为它们是一个概率分布。
The four numbers add up to one, because they form a probability distribution.
这就是语言模型的全部秘密：输入一段文本，输出词表上的一个分布。
That is the whole secret of a language model: text in, a distribution over the vocabulary out.
注意两个细节，它们后面会变得非常重要。
Two details matter, and both will become important later.
第一，输出是分布，不是一个词。选哪个词，是后面的采样策略决定的。
First, the output is a distribution, not a word. The choice is made by a sampling strategy, covered later.
这也解释了，为什么同一个问题问两次，答案可能不一样。
That also explains why the same question asked twice can get different answers.
第二，上文可以任意长。而这个承诺，正是 Transformer 要解决的问题。
Second, the context can be arbitrarily long. That promise is exactly what the Transformer was built to keep.
模型一次只预测一个词。那整句话的概率怎么算？
The model predicts one word at a time. So how do we get the probability of a whole sentence?
用概率论的链式法则，也就是高中学过的乘法公式，反复用。
Use the chain rule of probability: the multiplication rule from high school, applied again and again.
「我养了一只猫」的概率，等于每个词在它前面所有词条件下的概率，连乘起来。
The probability of "I keep a cat" is each word's probability given everything before it, multiplied together.
写成公式：从第一个词到第 T 个词，每一步条件概率的乘积。
In symbols: the product of the conditional probability at every step, from the first word to word T.
这种用自己前面的输出，当作下一步输入的生成方式，叫自回归。
Generating by feeding your own output back in as the next input is called autoregression.
语言模型就像一座桥，每次只往前挪一步。
A language model is like a bridge you cross one step at a time.
整句话的概率，就是每一步概率的连乘。
The probability of the sentence is the product of the probability of each step.
但很多个小于一的数相乘，会迅速变成零，这叫下溢。
But multiplying many numbers below one quickly collapses to zero. That is underflow.
所以实际计算时取对数，把连乘变成连加。
So in practice we take logarithms, turning the product into a sum.
对数在这里不是装饰。下一节你会看到，它恰好对应信息量。
The logarithm is not decoration. Next, you will see that it measures information.
那么，这些概率是怎么来的？历史上先后有两代做法。
So where do these probabilities come from? History offers two generations of answers.
第一代是数数，叫 n-gram 模型。
The first generation simply counted. These are n-gram models.
想知道「我养了一只」后面跟「猫」的概率，就去数这个组合在文本库里出现了多少次。
To estimate the probability of "cat" after "I keep a", count how often that combination appears in a corpus.
为了不让历史太长、一次都数不到，通常只回看最近 n 减一个词。
To avoid histories too long to ever be seen, it looks back only n minus one words.
它有两个致命伤。
It has two fatal weaknesses.
第一是稀疏：语言组合是无穷的，没见过的组合，概率就是零。
First, sparsity: word combinations are endless, and an unseen combination gets probability zero.
第二是不共享：在它眼里，「猫」和「狗」是两个毫不相干的计数。
Second, no sharing: to an n-gram model, "cat" and "dog" are two unrelated counts.
2003 年，Bengio 等人换了个方向：给每个词一个向量。
In 2003, Bengio and colleagues changed direction: give every word a vector.
相似的词，向量也相似；再用神经网络，算出下一个词的概率。
Similar words get similar vectors, and a neural network turns them into next-word probabilities.
一句话：n-gram 在记忆组合，神经语言模型在学习关系。
In one line: n-grams memorize combinations; neural language models learn relationships.
见过「我养了一只猫」，它自然也会给「我养了一只狗」不低的概率。
Having seen "I keep a cat", it naturally gives "I keep a dog" a decent probability too.
而这张「词向量到神经网络」的图，就是十七年后 GPT 的骨架。
And that diagram, vectors into a network, is the skeleton of GPT seventeen years later.
模型给出一组概率。怎么判断它猜得好不好？
The model outputs a distribution. How do we judge how well it guessed?
先从「意外」说起。
Start with surprise.
明天下雨的概率是 0.99，真下雨了，你不意外。
If rain tomorrow has probability 0.99, rain does not surprise you.
概率是 0.01，真下雨了，你很意外。
If the probability is 0.01, rain surprises you a lot.
所以意外程度，应该是概率的减函数。
So surprise should decrease as probability increases.
而且两个独立事件同时发生，意外应该等于各自意外之和。
And for two independent events, surprise should add up.
满足这两条的，本质上只有一个函数：负 log p。
Essentially one function satisfies both: minus log p.
这叫信息量。概率为一，信息量为零；概率趋近于零，信息量趋于无穷。
This is information content. Probability one gives zero; probability near zero gives near infinity.
把每种结果的意外，按概率平均，就是熵。
Average that surprise over outcomes, weighted by probability, and you get entropy.
公平硬币的熵是一比特；永远正面的硬币，熵是零。
A fair coin has one bit of entropy. A coin that always lands heads has zero.
现在是关键的一步。
Now comes the key step.
真实世界有一个分布 p，模型给出一个分布 q。
The world has a true distribution p. The model gives a distribution q.
用 q 去编码来自 p 的事件，平均意外程度，就是交叉熵。
Encoding events from p with q gives an average surprise: the cross-entropy.
它等于 p 自己的熵，加上一个叫 KL 散度的东西。
It equals the entropy of p, plus a term called the KL divergence.
KL 散度衡量两个分布的差异，永远非负。
KL divergence measures the gap between two distributions, and is never negative.
而 p 的熵是数据本身的性质，不随模型变。
The entropy of p belongs to the data, and does not change with the model.
所以最小化交叉熵，就是最小化 KL 散度，也就是让模型分布尽量接近真实分布。
So minimizing cross-entropy means minimizing KL divergence: moving the model distribution toward the truth.
几乎所有的语言模型，都用交叉熵当损失函数。
Almost every language model uses cross-entropy as its loss.
回到刚才的四词表。真实答案是猫，模型给了 0.60，交叉熵约等于 0.51 奈特。
Back to the four-word vocabulary: answer cat, model says 0.60, cross-entropy is about 0.51 nats.
如果真实答案是车，模型只给了 0.02，交叉熵约等于 3.91。
If the answer is car and the model gives only 0.02, cross-entropy is about 3.91.
猜错的代价，是猜对的七点七倍。
Being wrong here costs 7.7 times as much as being right.
交叉熵对「自信地猜错」，惩罚极重。
Cross-entropy punishes confident mistakes very heavily.
把奈特翻译成人话：取 e 的指数，得到困惑度。
To translate nats into plain language, exponentiate: that gives perplexity.
1.67 的困惑度，意思是平均在不到两个词之间犹豫。
A perplexity of 1.67 means the model hesitates between fewer than two words on average.
如果对五万个词完全均匀地乱猜，困惑度正好是五万。
Guessing uniformly among fifty thousand words gives a perplexity of exactly fifty thousand.
把交叉熵画成曲线：横轴是模型给正确答案的概率 q，纵轴是 −log q。
Plot cross-entropy: the x-axis is the probability q the model gives the correct answer; the y-axis is −log q.
q 越接近零，曲线越陡；KL 就是交叉熵高出熵的那一段。
As q approaches zero, the curve gets steeper; KL is the part of cross-entropy above entropy.
交叉熵等于熵加 KL。训练要压掉的，就是 KL 这一段。
Cross-entropy equals entropy plus KL. Training squeezes down that KL part.
把上面串起来，训练目标就很自然了。
Put it all together, and the training objective writes itself.
调整参数，让真实的下一个词，在模型分布下的平均负对数概率最小。
Tune the parameters so the true next word has the lowest average negative log probability.
这个式子还有第二个身份：最大似然估计。
This expression has a second identity: maximum likelihood estimation.
因为最小化负对数似然，等价于最大化似然。
Minimizing negative log-likelihood is the same as maximizing likelihood.
也就是，让模型认为训练语料尽可能可能发生。
In other words, make the training corpus as likely as possible under the model.
从信息论看，这叫最小化交叉熵；从统计学看，这叫最大似然。
Information theory calls it minimizing cross-entropy; statistics calls it maximum likelihood.
同一件事的两种语言，会贯穿整门课。
Two languages for one thing, and this pattern runs through the whole course.
至于具体怎么调参数，是下一章的主题。
How to actually tune those parameters is the next chapter.
模型最后吐出的，其实不是概率，而是一组任意实数，叫 logit。
What the model finally emits is not a probability but a set of arbitrary real numbers, called logits.
把它变成概率，用 softmax。
Turn them into probabilities with softmax.
每个 logit 先取指数，再除以所有指数之和。
Exponentiate each logit, then divide by the sum of all exponentials.
分母里多了一个温度参数，控制分布的锋利程度。
The denominator includes a temperature parameter that controls how sharp the distribution is.
温度趋近于零，几乎全给最大的 logit，输出确定。
As temperature approaches zero, almost all mass goes to the largest logit, and output becomes deterministic.
温度等于一，是原始分布；大于一，分布变平，冷门词也有机会。
At one you get the original distribution. Above one it flattens, giving rare words a chance.
这跟统计力学里的玻尔兹曼分布完全同构：logit 对应负能量，温度对应温度。
This is exactly the Boltzmann distribution: logits are negative energy, temperature is temperature.
只看两个候选词：横轴是 logit 差，纵轴是较高那个的概率。
Take just two candidates: the x-axis is the logit difference, the y-axis is the probability of the higher one.
温度越小，曲线越像台阶；温度越大，曲线越平缓。
The lower the temperature, the more the curve looks like a step; the higher it is, the flatter the curve.
有了分布，还要决定怎么选词，这叫解码。
With a distribution in hand, we still choose a word. That step is called decoding.
贪心，永远选概率最大的，确定但容易重复。
Greedy decoding always takes the top word: deterministic, but prone to repetition.
纯采样，按概率抽，多样但可能离谱。
Pure sampling draws by probability: diverse, but sometimes wild.
top-k 只在最高的 k 个里抽；top-p 只在累积概率达到 p 的最小集合里抽。
Top-k samples from the k most likely words; top-p from the smallest set whose mass reaches p.
这些都是推理时的旋钮，不改模型本身。
All of these are knobs at inference time. They do not change the model itself.
最后，看看这个目标的天花板和地板。
Finally, look at the floor and the ceiling of this objective.
地板是：只会预测下一个词的模型，在 2003 年只能做很有限的事。
The floor: in 2003, a model that only predicts the next word could do very little.
它需要大量数据、大量算力，还需要一个能记住长上文的架构。
It needed lots of data, lots of compute, and an architecture that could remember a long context.
天花板是一个值得反复思考的问题。
The ceiling is a question worth returning to.
要准确预测「这道积分等于」，模型必须真的会算积分吗？
To predict "this integral equals", must the model actually know how to integrate?
还是只要记住，这类题后面常跟哪个数字就够了？
Or is it enough to remember which numbers tend to follow such problems?
答案是：在训练数据覆盖的范围内，记忆就够了；一旦超出，就必须学会规则。
The answer: inside the training distribution, memory suffices. Outside it, the model must learn rules.
而学会规则这件事，会在规模变大时自发发生。
And learning rules happens spontaneously as scale grows.
这就是为什么，一个看似平庸的目标，最终逼出了推理。
That is why such a plain objective eventually forced reasoning into existence.
但也别过度浪漫化。它优化的是文本上的条件概率，不是世界的真相。
But do not romanticize it. It optimizes conditional probability over text, not the truth of the world.
这两者的缝隙，就是幻觉的来源。
The gap between the two is where hallucinations come from.
这一章，我们有了目标函数。
This chapter gave us an objective function.
但还没有回答：参数怎么自动变好？
But we have not answered how parameters improve by themselves.
下一章讲梯度下降与反向传播。
The next chapter covers gradient descent and backpropagation.
全课程第一个陡坡，也是整个深度学习的发动机。
The first steep climb of the course, and the engine of all deep learning.
第二章，梯度与反向传播。我们下期见。
Chapter two: gradients and backpropagation. See you next time.
